hypotheses.title: Inverted Supply Chain Spillover with 3-Day Volume Damping (Fast Horizon Calibration)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Batch 233 and 234 proved that customer shock mean-reversion is an agile 4-to-5 day phenomenon (Sharpe 1.51 at 5d vs 0.89 at 10d). To compress turnover from 48% to ~18% without diluting the 4-day signal, we apply short 3-day linear volume damping alongside platform Decay 8. This preserves the agile customer signal while smoothing daily execution churn, targeting Sharpe >= 1.45 and Fitness >= 1.50.
confounders: Sudden sector-wide macro liquidations that override supplier-customer relationship links
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if 3-day volume damping fails to reduce turnover or causes Sharpe to drop below 1.25.

hypotheses.title: Inverse Volume Scaled Supply Chain Spillover (Ratio Smoothing)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Instead of linear subtraction (1 - rank), dividing by (1 + rank) smooths the sensitivity to extreme daily volume spikes and produces gentler portfolio weight adjustments. When simulated with Decay 8, this directly dampens daily churn while keeping the 5-day inverted customer shock engine fully intact.
confounders: Extreme illiquid stocks where volume / adv20 denominator approaches zero
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if ratio scaling weakens signal responsiveness during major customer earnings announcements.

hypotheses.title: Virgin model16 Earnings Certainty and Composite Quality Synergy
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Explores completely virgin model16 composite fields with 100% coverage across TOP3000. Inverting the polarity (-earnings_certainty_rank_derivative) penalizes accounting accruals and volatile earnings streams, while -composite_factor_score_derivative rewards multi-factor operational momentum. Cross-sectional ranking within subindustries ensures balanced sector allocation.
confounders: Speculative momentum regimes where unprofitable firms with low earnings certainty lead the market
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high earnings certainty firms underperform low-quality peers during risk-on market rallies.
